label: In an English news report or story narrative, the word that tells how an ongoing situation runs over time: it drags on or is still under way ('continuing to', 'now in its third week', 'remains open a year later', 'detectives are still seeking'), ends, often without an outcome ('ended without', 'could end before'), or is put off again ('postponed again', 'delayed once more'); personal plans and errands, instructions ('stir until it thickens'), film plot summaries, market figures and static facts stay weak; a space-object flyby headline ('Asteroid Flyby') also fires

probed_before.source: this checkout's .probe-log, before the pre-registration commit

qc.label_under_test: in a reported news or story narrative, the word that tells how an ongoing situation's course runs: it keeps going, ends (often without an outcome), stalls, or is put off or decided ('continuing to', 'now in its third week', 'ended without any trace', 'postponed again', 'has decided to', 'until', 'before'); static facts, market figures, casual first-person plans and instructions ('bake until golden') stay weak; a space-rock headline ('Asteroid Flyby') also fires
